title: Proportional Hold-and-Release Admission with Conditional Fidelity Tiers
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Design and implement a 'proportional hold-and-release' admission controller that enforces fair shedding across priorities and tenants while enabling conditional fidelity degradation modes. Integrates with region-level circuit breakers and multi-region failover routing. Goal: preserve P0/P1 SLOs under overload by holding lower-priority requests in proportional reservoirs, releasing them when capacity returns or spilling them to fallback fidelity (cached/compressed/partial response) or alternate regions.
discussion: 2026-02-20 Aisha Patel: Initial RFC drafted. Core idea: combine token-reservoirs per priority band with a global occupancy signal to compute proportional holds. Include conditional fidelity tiers as a graceful fallback instead of outright rejects.
2026-02-24 Marco Nguyen: Prototype admission hook implemented in local dev runtime. Basic token reservoir and hold queue works; need fairness test harness to avoid starvation of mid-priority tenants.

2026-03-01 Elena Rossi (Design): UX for console needs a clear way to show held request counts, expected release windows, and fidelity tier applied. Suggested exposing 'expected fidelity' in request traces.

2026-03-03 SRE review (Jonas Meyer): Concern about coupling holds with long-tailed workloads; suggested max-hold-time per request and circuit-breaker short-circuit to cached responses beyond threshold.

2026-03-07 Marco Nguyen: Integrated with region circuit-breaker API. When CB trips for a region, controller increases spillover probability and moves held low-priority tokens to alternate-region routing. Observed 12% latency impact on P1 in synthetic failover test; tuning required.

2026-03-10 Aisha Patel: Decided to implement starvation protection: every N seconds release a minimum token fraction for each non-empty priority band. Also added metrics to measure 'time-held' histogram and 'fidelity-applied' counters.
acceptance_criteria: Admission controller enforces proportional holding across at least three priority bands (P0,P1,P2) and exposes per-priority held_count metric.
When cluster region is under overload, P0 P95 latency remains within configured SLO (<= 150ms for synthetic workload) while P2 requests are held or downgraded to conditional fidelity.
Conditional fidelity modes implemented: (1) cached response return, (2) compressed/trimmed token output, (3) model-slimming fallback. Fidelity selection is configurable and instrumented.
Integration test for multi-region failover: when primary region CB trips, at least 80% of held P1/P2 tokens spill to configured secondary region within 5s without violating P0 SLOs in either region.
Runbook steps documented for operators: how to adjust hold thresholds, release windows, and fidelity mappings; postmortem checklist included.
Dashboard panels exist showing held counts, average hold time, fidelity distribution, spillover rate, and per-priority SLO burn rates.
End-to-end tests and synthetic load experiments included in the PR and green in CI (unit + integration harness).
